input.quote: (h) Neither Party may assign (voluntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise) this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction.
input.rationale: Section (h) gives AP the affiliate/successor carve-out we require: AP may assign without consent to an affiliate, to a purchaser of all or substantially all relevant assets, or to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation, and all other assignments require consent that may not be unreasonably withheld. The restriction is mutual, and a search of the termination and other operative provisions found no change-of-control concept anywhere in the Agreement, so Kubient has no termination or re-pricing right on an AP change of control. This meets the preferred position on the material terms and sits at or above the fallback (mutual assignment to successors with consent not unreasonably withheld). Two preferred sub-elements are absent but immaterial: there is no express bar on Kubient assigning to an AP competitor, and Kubient enjoys the same consent-free carve-out AP does. Noted, not redlined.
